links.outcome: Predictive discrimination on internal versus temporally separate external validation data
links.effect: AUC decreased from 0.886 internally to 0.786 externally; ΔAUC was 0.100. External validation used data from 2021 to 2022.
links.quote: Internal validation showed an AUC of 0.886, while external validation showed an AUC of 0.786, with a ΔAUC of 0.100, indicating the model’s consistency and generalizability across different datasets ( Supplementary Figure S4 ).

links.outcome: Comparative discrimination of candidate models predicting prescriber acceptance
links.effect: Among 11 models, Random Forest achieved AUC = 0.893, compared with LightGBM = 0.797, DT = 0.780, XGBoost = 0.777, and GBM = 0.773.
links.quote: Among the 11 ML models, the RF model had the best predictive performance in terms of AUC (AUC = 0.893), followed by the LightGBM model (AUC = 0.797), DT model (AUC = 0.780), XGBoost model (AUC = 0.777), and GBM model (AUC = 0.773) ( Figure 3A ).

links.outcome: Prescriber acceptance, hospital stay, costs, and adverse drug reactions after SMPOP implementation
links.effect: Uncontrolled pre/post: acceptance 40.63% to 71.30%; stay 13 to 7 days; hospitalization costs 32,263.42 to 20,842.89 RMB; medication costs 7847.67 to 4,712.92 RMB (p < 0.001); ADRs 0.4% to 0.18% (p = 0.095).
links.quote: Compared to the ML development period and external validation period, the acceptance rate of pharmacists’ recommendations in the post-implementation evaluation period increased from 40.63% to 71.30%, the length of stay was reduced from 13 days (IQR: 8, 22) ( P < 0.001) to 7 days (IQR: 9, 15) ( p < 0.001), total hospitalization costs decreased from 32,263.42 RMB (IQR: 16,880.46,68,921.29) ( p < 0.001) to 20,842.89 RMB (IQR: 13,516.59, 32,055.51) ( p < 0.001), cost of medication decreased from 7847.67 RMB (IQR: 3815.45,19,980.16) ( p < 0.001) to 4,712.92 RMB (IQR: 2866.63, 7716.55) ( p < 0.001), and the ADR rate was reduced from 0.4% to 0.18% ( p = 0.095).

links.outcome: Predictive model performance on a temporally later dataset
links.effect: The selected random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.786 on a temporally later validation dataset, a decrease from 0.886 during internal validation.
links.quote: Internal validation showed an AUC of 0.886, while external validation showed an AUC of 0.786, with a ΔAUC of 0.100, indicating the model’s consistency and generalizability across different datasets ( Supplementary Figure S4 ).

links.effect: The random forest model outperformed 10 alternative machine learning models, achieving the highest AUC (0.893) compared to the next best models like LightGBM (0.797) and Decision Tree (0.780).
links.quote: Among the 11 ML models, the RF model had the best predictive performance in terms of AUC (AUC = 0.893), followed by the LightGBM model (AUC = 0.797), DT model (AUC = 0.780), XGBoost model (AUC = 0.777), and GBM model (AUC = 0.773) ( Figure 3A ).

links.outcome: Clinical outcomes and costs after AI deployment
links.effect: After implementing the AI-assisted service, recommendation acceptance rose to 71.30%, median length of stay dropped to 7 days, and both total and medication costs decreased significantly.
links.quote: Compared to the ML development period and external validation period, the acceptance rate of pharmacists’ recommendations in the post-implementation evaluation period increased from 40.63% to 71.30%, the length of stay was reduced from 13 days (IQR: 8, 22) ( P < 0.001) to 7 days (IQR: 9, 15) ( p < 0.001), total hospitalization costs decreased from 32,263.42 RMB (IQR: 16,880.46,68,921.29) ( p < 0.001) to 20,842.89 RMB (IQR: 13,516.59, 32,055.51) ( p < 0.001), cost of medication decreased from 7847.67 RMB (IQR: 3815.45,19,980.16) ( p < 0.001) to 4,712.92 RMB (IQR: 2866.63, 7716.55) ( p < 0.001), and the ADR rate was reduced from 0.4% to 0.18% ( p = 0.095).
